original_context:
The Lilac Fire in San Diego County has led to a significant crisis, with thousands ordered to evacuate due to the rapidly spreading fire, which quickly grew to 50 acres. At least 63 homes and other structures have been destroyed, and an additional 45 have been damaged. The fire has resulted in six reported injuries, including three civilians with burn injuries and one civilian suffering from smoke inhalation. The fire has also caused water supplies to be contaminated, and there is a need for food, water, and supplies for both people and animals. 

Emergency services are actively responding, with 700 firefighters on the job, supported by 100 fire engines, 15 helicopters, 7 air tankers, and additional assistance expected from 2 Navy and 2 Marine helicopters. Despite these efforts, the exact locations of the fires are not being reported by the news. The situation is exacerbated by dry weather and high winds, with gusts predicted to reach the strength of a Category 1 hurricane in mountainous areas.

Approximately 19,300 people are without power, as San Diego Gas and Electric has cut off power to prevent downed power lines from sparking further fires. Traffic disruptions include road closures on Green Canyon Road in Fallbrook and all roads in and out of Bonsall, as well as traffic lights out at Willow Rd in San Diego. 

Evacuation shelters have been set up, with nearly 900 people currently in shelters. Shelters in Carlsbad and Oceanside filled overnight, prompting the opening of a new shelter at Palomar College in San Marcos. The Stagecoach Park shelter is in need of donations, and the Del Mar Fairgrounds requires water and assistance. 

Special needs elderly individuals and 500 horses at the San Luis Rey Training Center need evacuation. Schools in the VUSD district have been canceled, and the Interfaiths Libby Lake Service Center is closed due to the fire. The crisis has prompted declarations to free state resources, including the National Guard, to support response efforts. Hazards from the fire include asbestos, heavy metals, and by-products of plastic combustion.

Evacuation centers are open at Del Mar Fairgrounds, Palomar College, and other locations, with the Del Mar Fairgrounds also accommodating large animals. Volunteers and supplies, such as apples, carrots, dog food, and bridles, are needed for horses.

The San Diego Foundation has activated a Regional Disaster Fund to support wildfire response and recovery. Governor Jerry Brown has issued an emergency proclamation for San Diego County. The Red Cross continues to provide shelters and Disaster Health Services for those affected. The community is rallying to support evacuees, with many displaced and in need of shelter.

original_context: A massive explosion occurred in Beirut, Lebanon, on Tuesday, causing widespread destruction and devastation. The blast, which sent a giant mushroom cloud into the sky, was caused by approximately 2,750 tonnes of ammonium nitrate stored in a warehouse at the port. The explosion flattened much of the port, damaged buildings throughout the capital, and shook distant buildings, creating panic and chaos. The incident resulted in at least 100 deaths and over 4,000 injuries, with many bodies still buried in the rubble. More than 300,000 people have been displaced, and the cost of damages is estimated to be between $3 billion and $5 billion. The air is contaminated, and residents have been warned about toxic gases released by the explosion. Search and rescue efforts are underway, with volunteers needed for relief operations, including clearing debris and donating blood. The Lebanese authorities were warned about the hazardous materials stored at the port, and an investigation into possible negligence is ongoing. The Prime Minister of Lebanon has promised to hold those responsible accountable. International aid and support are being mobilized to assist the affected population.

original_context: Severe weather swept through the South on Thursday, resulting in the deaths of at least seven people in Oklahoma, Texas, and Louisiana. Among the victims were a factory worker killed by an apparent tornado, a man whose car was blown off the road, and another man swept away in a flood while retrieving a trash can. The hardest-hit area was Onalaska, Texas, where a tornado damaged 306 homes and destroyed 173. Three people were killed in Onalaska, including in the Yaupon Cove subdivision. The National Weather Service confirmed tornado touchdowns in Madill, Oklahoma, and Tallahassee, Florida, with multiple tornado warnings issued across Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana, and Florida. Severe Thunderstorm and Tornado Watches are in effect for various regions, including central Florida and parts of southeast Oklahoma, northeast Texas, northwest Louisiana, and southwest Arkansas. More than 150,000 businesses and homes from Texas to Georgia are without power. Evacuations are needed, and volunteers are requested to assist with disaster relief efforts, including providing shelter, water, and clothing. Road damage has been reported on Moro Road and Back Road BBQ, and several areas are blocked due to debris. Emergency management agencies are providing assistance, and evacuation centers are set up in the Northeast, North, and Central regions. The severe weather has also led to the closure of drive-up COVID-19 testing sites and city park facilities.
